 Live Updates Updated Tue, Nov 3 2026 11:26 PM EST Share Share Article via Facebook Share Article via Twitter Share Article via LinkedIn Share Article via Email Stock futures fall on speculation Democrats to win big in midterms, slow data center buildout: Live updates
 Sean Conlon Traders work on the floor at the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE) in New York City, US, November 2, 2026. Brendan Mcdermid | Reuters Stock futures dropped on Tuesday evening as traders speculated that Democrats were headed for majority control of Congress and some key gubernatorial wins in the 2026 U.S. midterm elections .
 Futures tied to the S&P 500 traded 1.3% lower, while Nasdaq-100 futures shed 2.2%. Futures tied to the Dow Jones Industrial Average were down 410 points, or 0.8%.
 Kalshi odds for Democratic Senate control increased to above 99%, showing traders were increasingly betting on a big night for Democrats. Odds for Democratic control of the House, which was largely expected, jumped to 99% for Democrats. CNBC's Election Desk projects that Democrats will win the U.S. House. Democrats are also pacing to gain control of the Senate.
 Texas Democratic governor candidate Gina Hinojosa is the winner over Republican incumbent Greg Abbott, The Associated Press projected. Hinojosa has pledged a moratorium on data centers in the key tech hub.
 If Democrats are able to secure a sizable majority in the Senate — the so-called blue wave scenario — the market and especially stocks related to the artificial intelligence buildout could come under pressure , according to some on Wall Street. Investors fear a big Democratic win could mean more restrictions on data centers nationwide. AI-linked stocks have already pulled back in recent weeks on concern about a slowing pace in data-center spending.
 Big Tech shares Microsoft , Amazon and Nvidia were all trading lower in extended trading. High-risk data center play CoreWeave was down 6% in Robinhood overnight trading. Elon Musk's SpaceX was also off by 6% on Robinhood.
 Equities "trended lower as it's looked more likely that Democrats are going to pick up the House and most likely the Senate," said Anthony Saglimbene, chief market strategist at Ameriprise Financial.
 "I think it'll be more interesting on how the governorships go," Saglimbene added. "If you get some governorships that are Democratic, what does that mean for the data center buildout, which has already seen a lot of skepticism over the last couple weeks in terms of the hyperscaler capex spending."
 Stock Chart Icon Stock chart icon S&P 500 futures, intraday To be sure, the polls have yet to fully close in all states. Election nights have often shown wild swings in markets. Many investors also believe any market move from this election would be short lived. 
 AMD shares initially surged double digits in post-market action after the company, a key player in the AI trade, reported third-quarter earnings and revenue that blew past analyst expectations. The stock was last up about 3% higher as stock market futures gave up their gains.
 On the overall market, investors believe a blue wave would also be a headwind as it likely rules out any more business-friendly policies like tax breaks and possibly increases scrutiny on industries like banking. 
 Renewable shares like solar stocks traded higher in the post market on speculation a Democratic majority in Congress would halt policies by President Donald Trump taken against the industry. The Invesco Solar ETF was up 3.5% in Robinhood trading.
 As equity futures fell into the red, Treasury yields moved lower, with the 10-year Treasury note yield dropping more than 4 basis points to 4.904%. Futures on the Cboe Volatility Index fear gauge increased, rising above 20 , as investors braced for a pullback.
 25 Min Ago Trump Media & Technology shares drop as Democratic sweep seems more likely
 Shares of Trump Media & Technology declined more than 7% in overnight trading on Robinhood as the 2026 midterm elections appear poised to conclude with a blue wave.
 The stock moved lower after CNBC's Election Desk projected that Democrats are going to win the House. The party was also on track to take Senate control from Republicans.
 President Donald Trump said in a Truth Social post late Tuesday, "I wasn't on the Ballot and if I was, we would have won IN A LANDSLIDE!"
 — Sean Conlon 
 37 Min Ago Japan's Nikkei plunges over 4% to lowest since May as U.S. midterm election jitters rattle AI stocks
 Japan's Nikkei 225 plunged more than 4% on Wednesday, leading losses across Asia-Pacific markets as renewed jitters over artificial intelligence stocks weighed on investor sentiment amid uncertainty surrounding the U.S. midterm elections.
 The benchmark declined 4.45% to its lowest since May. Technology and energy stocks led declines in the benchmark, according to data from LSEG, while the broader Topix index tumbled more than 3%. 
 The sell-off came as investors weighed the prospect of tighter restrictions on data-center development under a potential Democratic-controlled Congress, adding to concerns over the outlook for AI-related spending.
 —Lee Ying Shan 
 1 Hour Ago Treasury yields slide
 Treasury yields fell as investors sought shelter from a sell-off in equity futures sparked by potential big victories from Democrats in the U.S. midterm elections.
 The benchmark 10-year Treasury note yield dropped nearly 5 basis points to 4.902%. The 30-year bond yield slid 5.29%, and the shorter-term 2-year note yield pulled back 6 basis points to 4.55%. Read more .
 Stock Chart Icon Stock chart icon US10Y, 1-day — Fred Imbert 
 1 Hour Ago SpaceX shares fall as Hinojosa continues lead in Texas governor election
 Nikolas Kokovlis | Nurphoto | Getty Images Shares of SpaceX fell more than 6% on Robinhood overnight trading as Democratic candidate Gina Hinojosa continued her lead over Republican incumbent Greg Abbott in the Texas gubernatorial race.
 "Let's watch SpaceX. Let's watch Tesla . This is Elon Musk-land now. There are a lot of California companies that moved to Texas, thinking, 'All right, we're going to get out of this blue state and go somewhere safe,' and now it's proven that it isn't," Jay Woods, Freedom Capital Markets' chief market strategist, said in an interview with CNBC.
 "You want to watch a lot of these Texas companies that moved there," he stressed.
 Musk said that he was going to move the headquarters of both companies to Texas from California back in 2024. Tesla shares were down more than 4% on Robinhood.
 — Sean Conlon 
 2 Hours Ago Investors watching Texas for AI trade clues
 Investors were focusing on the results of the Texas gubernatorial race for clues about the AI trade because the state represents an outsized portion of data center capacity. Democratic candidate Gina Hinojosa has an early lead over Republican incumbent Greg Abbott. Hinojosa is calling for an immediate moratorium on data centers in the state and an end any tax incentives for the build-out.
 "The one thing that could really end up moving stuff though would be if Abbott were to lose Texas," said Scott Ladner, chief investment officer of Horizon Investments. "Because there is a legitimate question about, where do you build these data centers?"
 "Texas is a fertile ground for that. And if he were to lose, I think that fertile ground is largely barren. So, that's going to be a challenge. And so the AI trade — at least for next couple days — does hinge on does Abbott win or not," Ladner added. 
 Texas represents about 27% of U.S. data center gigawatts, estimates Wells Fargo.
 — John Melloy and Sarah Min 
 3 Hours Ago Volatility spurred by the midterms could be an opportunity for investors, strategist says
 People vote at a polling location on Election Day during the midterm elections in New York City on November 3, 2026. Timothy A. Clary | Afp | Getty Images Any big surprises out of the 2026 midterm elections could mean buying opportunities for investors, according to Angelo Kourkafas, senior strategist at Edward Jones.
 "The results could act as a clearing event removing some uncertainty, though developments around the AI theme and geopolitics are the primary forces driving markets heading into the final two months of the year," he said.
 However, he added: "If we do see election-driven volatility it may present an opportunity for long-term investors to lean into it."
 — Sean Conlon 
 3 Hours Ago HSBC issues $4.25 billion in two-part debt offering
 HSBC said on Wednesday it had issued $4.25 billion in senior unsecured debt in two tranches, including $1.75 billion in notes due in 2032 at 5.819% fixed-rate/floating-rate and another $2.5 billion in notes maturing in 2037 at 6.262%. 
 Europe's largest bank, which plans to list the securities on the New York Stock Exchange, did not specify how the funds raised would be deployed.
 — Lee Ying Shan 
 3 Hours Ago VIX futures rise above 20
 Cboe Volatility Index (VIX) futures moved higher on Tuesday evening as U.S. equity futures came under pressure amid results from the midterm elections.
 Futures tied to the VIX, otherwise referred to as Wall Street's " fear gauge ," were last seen trading at 20.90.
 A move above 20 tends to be a key level signaling heightened angst among investors in the market.
 — Sean Conlon 
 4 Hours Ago How the S&P 500 has performed after midterms
 Investors are on edge as polls across the U.S. begin closing in an election that could bring gridlock to government. But if history is any indication, they may have little to worry about. 
 A CNBC analysis of S&P 500 returns after elections from 1980 through 2024 shows the benchmark rose an average of 0.2% one day after the election and 1.1% in the month following. One year out, the benchmark averages a 13.8% return and rose in 91% of cases. That's including general elections. 
 Looking at just post-midterm returns, the record is even stronger. The S&P 500 has risen after each of the last 11 midterm elections between 1982 and 2022. One year out, the index returns 13.7% on average. 
 Read the full story here .
 — Deena Zaidi and Nick Wells 
 4 Hours Ago Solar ETF extends gains in after hours trading
 watch now VIDEO 1:03 01:03 Options Action: Bulls take a shine to solar stocks Options Action The Invesco Solar ETF (TAN) rose by 1.3% in after hours trading on Tuesday, extending gains from the regular session when the ETF rallied 3% as traders bet on stocks most likely to benefit from Democrat leadership. 
 Options trading in solar companies surged Tuesday, following a five-month selloff for the group. Volume in the Invesco Solar ETF (TAN) surged to 40 times higher than usual, according to Cboe LiveVol data. The fund, which typically trades fewer than 500 contracts a day the past month, traded more than 20,000 contracts by midday, and 99% of them were calls. 
 Stock Chart Icon Stock chart icon TAN, 1-day — Sarah Min, Oliver Renick 
 4 Hours Ago Chip stocks give up gains
 Shares of key chipmakers gave up their initial gains on Tuesday evening, moving into negative territory.
 Intel fell more than 1%, while Micron Technology dropped around 1%. Nvidia also fell nearly 1%.
 The VanEck Semiconductor ETF (SMH) and the iShares Semiconductor ETF (SOXX) each dropped almost 1% as well.
 Stock Chart Icon Stock chart icon SMH, 1-day — Sean Conlon 
 4 Hours Ago South Korea's Kospi gains 3% as chip stocks jump
 Asia-Pacific markets started the trading day mixed.
 South Korea's Kospi jumped 2.95%, while the small-cap Kosdaq added 1.85%. 
 Japan's  Nikkei 225 opened flat, while the Topix added 0.43%.
 Australia's S&P/ASX 200 was down 0.45%.
 — Lee Ying Shan 
 5 Hours Ago CVS Health rises on WSJ report that it will split off its retail pharmacy business
 CVS Health Corp. signage on the floor of the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE) in New York, US, on Monday, July 28, 2025. Michael Nagle | Bloomberg | Getty Images Shares of CVS Health advanced in extended trading on the back of a report in The Wall Street Journal that the company will separate its retail pharmacy business.
 The split will turn CVS into two separate companies, people familiar with the matter told the Journal. Both entities will be publicly traded, with the division expected to take place in the first half of 2028.
 Stock Chart Icon Stock chart icon CVS Health in the past day Shares of CVS were last up around 1% in after hours.
 — Darla Mercado 
 5 Hours Ago Asia-Pacific markets set for mixed open as U.S. chip stocks recover 
 Asia-Pacific markets were set for a mixed open Wednesday, as investors assessed a rebound in Wall Street technology stocks while awaiting the results of the U.S. midterm elections.
 Futures for Japan's  Nikkei 225  in Chicago were at 63,410, while in Osaka they were last at 63,090 compared with the index's previous close of 63,081.86.
 Futures for Hong Kong's Hang Seng index last traded at 23,400 compared with the index's last close of 23,525.97.
 Australia's S&P/ASX 200 was down 0.5% in early trading.
 — Lee Ying Shan 
 5 Hours Ago Stocks making the biggest moves after hours: AMD, Super Micro & more
 Lisa Su, chair and chief executive officer of Advanced Micro Devices Inc. (AMD), speaks during the company's Gamers Day event in Seoul, South Korea, on Wednesday, Oct. 7, 2026. SeongJoon Cho | Bloomberg | Getty Images A slate of stocks moved sharply in extended trading, largely driven by the latest earnings reports: 
 Advanced Micro Devices — The chipmaker jumped 7% after reporting stronger-than-expected third-quarter earnings . Adjusted earnings of $2.09 per share topped estimates for $1.95, according to analysts polled by LSEG. Revenue forecasts for the current quarter also came in above estimates
 Super Micro Computer — Shares of the server company jumped more than 9% after Super Micro earnings per share and revenue beat Wall Street estimates. For fiscal year 2027, the company expects net sales to range between $72 billion and $82 billion, above the LSEG consensus for $69.17 billion.
 Arista Networks — The cloud networking company gained 12% after current-quarter guidance topped estimates. Arista sees fourth-quarter earnings of $1.26 to $1.30 per share on revenue of $3.9 billion to $4.0 billion. Analysts surveyed by LSEG were looking for $1.15 per share and $3.60 billion.
 Read more about Tuesday's movers in extended trading here .
 — Darla Mercado 
 6 Hours Ago S&P 500, Nasdaq futures open higher
 Futures tied to the S&P 500 and Nasdaq-100 opened higher on Tuesday evening.
 S&P 500 futures rose 0.2%, while Nasdaq-100 futures gained 0.5%. However, Dow Jones Industrial Average futures lost 60 points, or 0.1%.
 — Sean Conlon
